messages:
anya: Heads-up — thinking about adding an explicit consent step in the console when delegating org-level service accounts to projects. Users keep surprising us by granting wide scopes without realizing quota/billing fallout. Want to brainstorm telemetry + rollout.
mike: +1. Can you sketch the UX you have in mind? is this a modal before finalizing a binding or a separate consent flow?
anya: Modal before finalize. Show affected project quotas, which models the SA can hit, and a checkbox: 'I understand this may affect billing and quotas.' Minimal friction.
lucas: Sounds right. From the platform side we need clear signals: bind_attempt, bind_success, bind_cancel while showing which quotas were in scope. We'll want attribution_id on the bind call.
sarah: Also add a simulation button — "preview impact" that runs a dry-run against quota calculator and returns estimated monthly token usage cost. avoids blind clicks. UX shouldn't block automation though.
priya: Important question: does this change require a new API header or change to token exchange? If console must call the backend to record consent we should persist consent events and attach them to the SA history.
anya: Yeah, we'll persist an audit event. Proposal: add a consent record object with fields (actor, timestamp, binding_details, scope_snapshot). Minimal schema.
mike: On telemetry — key metrics to watch during rollout: consent_accept_rate, consent_cancel_rate, post-bind_401_rate, attribution_mismatch_count, and average_time-to-bind. Also errors from the simulation.
lucas: For rollout, I suggest feature-flag + canary: 1% of orgs get the modal + telemetry; after 24h sanity bump to 10% and so on. For automation-heavy orgs, we provide an "allowlist" where the modal is suppressed if an org-admin pre-authorizes automation rules.
sarah: UX caveat: don't pop the modal for service tokens created via infra-as-code flows. We'll need a detection heuristic and an override. Maybe if request contains header `X-Automation-Flow: true` bypass the modal with extra audit log.
priya: Implementation detail — new header we can add: `X-Delegate-Consent: consent_id` once consent is recorded. Example:
```http
POST /v1/bindings
Authorization: Bearer ...
X-Delegate-Consent: cons_123abc
```
The backend verifies cons_123abc exists and matches actor + scope.
mike: Nice. That makes downstream routing deterministic for quota attribution.
anya: Who owns the console changes vs API changes? I'm happy to take console + audit storage. Priya/Platform own API header + validation.
priya: I'll add a small API proto change and a migration for consent records. Need to coordinate DB write pattern to avoid hot writes on bind path (write-ahead queue maybe).
lucas: Telemetry dashboards: I'll add a new panel in the auth/keys dashboard: consent_accept_rate over time, simulation_use_count, and top orgs by cancellations. Also set an alert if post-bind_401_rate spikes > 0.5%.
sarah: For rollout communications: small banner in console docs and an announcement in #product and #security. Also drafting copy for the modal that clearly states "this grants X access to Y" (no legalese).
anya: Can we gate the rollout on three safety checks: 1) simulation API latency < 300ms P95; 2) DB write errors < 0.1% in canary; 3) no increase in attribution_mismatch_count > baseline + 2 sigma.
mike: Agreed. I'll own alerting rules for those.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: feature-flag consent-modal v1 enabled in canary (1% orgs) at 4999990300 — rollout paused for telemetry review.
priya: I'll open a short PR for the header validation and a migration ticket. tagging @mike and @lucas for telemetry hooks.
anya: Great. I'll sketch modal copy and the simulation API contract by EOD. Thanks all :rocket:
